recipes.name: Peach Cheesecake
ingredients_raw: 1 (1.5 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix
1 (15 ounce) can canned peaches - drained with 3 tablespoons juice reserved

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Butter an 8-inch square baking dish.
Beat baking mix, milk, butter, vanilla pudding mix, and egg together in a large bowl with an electric mixer for 2 minutes; pour into the prepared baking dish.
Chop peaches; scatter over top of batter.

Beat cream cheese, ½ cup sugar, and reserved peach juice together in a medium bowl with an electric mixer until smooth; pour over peaches. Combine 1 tablespoon sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl; sprinkle over cream cheese mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until the center is set, 30 to 35 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Peach Cheesecake
raw_recipe.description: This no-crust peach cheesecake recipe features canned peaches baked in a vanilla pudding mix batter and covered with a cinnamon cream cheese topping.

review.reviewBody: what is baking mix in this receipe

I have had this recipe for years and it is always a favorite at my house or any home I take it to. I always double the recipe,bake in a 9x13x2 glass dish andrefrigerate after cooling to set the cream cheese filling. Plus, the cinnamon/sugar topping - I add more than called for. More is better!!

This recipe is great! My husband requested a peach cheesecake for his birthday and this one more than delivered. He asked for a second one to share with his family, and wanted FRESH peaches in it this time. After doing some research, I decided to try it. In order to remove the skin easily from fresh peaches, you need to boil the whole peach for about 30 to 40 SECONDS, then plunge them immediately into a bowl of very cold water. This allows air to get beneath the skin and it is easier to remove. Afterwards, I simply chopped them up and added them. I also changed the "baking mix" to white lily self-rising flour, and I took some juice from a can of peaches to add the right amount of peach juice. He and his family loved it, and are awaiting the next installment -- Thanks!

Made this today for Father's Day so I wanted it to be extra special; I had some blueberries that I'd just picked at a local farm and made a blueberry sauce as follows: 1 1/2 cups fresh blueberries, 1/4 cup water, 1/3 to 1/2 cup sugar, 1 tablespoon cornstarch, 1/4 teaspoon almond extract. Put berries and next 3 ingredients in a saucepan, bring to boil, stirring frequently until spoon is coated - approximately 20 to 35 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 1/4 teaspoon almond extract. Ladle a couple of heaping spoonfulls on individual servings of Peach Cheesecake. Very special indeed! Everyone love it! (Texture of 'cheesecake' more like a cobbler, but still very tasty!)

This is the first recipe I have ever reviewed. It is both quite easy to make and exceptionally delicious. It is peach season now, so I used just over 2 cups of fresh, organic peaches. I also sprinkled the peaches with sugar, let some juice come out, and used the juice to mix into the cream cheese. This is now my favorite dessert recipe for peach season, and is going to be hard to dethrone (although I am open to challenger suggestions).

P.S. "Baking mix" = Bisquick or the like (I used Bisquick and people did not guess it was Bisquick)

This recipe needs help. It may work better is you add 1 cup of milk to the pudding mix before adding bisquick. It was like paste until I added more milk. The crust came out rubbery following directions as they were. If you want a real cheescake effect beat in one egg to the topping,

This was a great recipe the only thing is i added was the left over peach juice i add to the crust mixture because it was a little thick and i used a 5.1 oz box of instant pudding it turned out great will definately make it again.:)
It rocks! This time I used cherry pie filling in place of the peaches and couple of tbsps of rum instead of peach juice.

Well, this is funny because I have had this recipe card in my recipe box for 15 YEARS and it is tattered as well. Except mine is called "Peaches and Cream Cheesecake". Every time I make this, the recipe is requested over and over. Now I lost my recipe box and while I somewhat remembered the recipe, I set out to find it. This is exactly like mine, except mine called for flour and added leavening, not baking mix. You can also use pineapple as well. I leave off the cinn-sugar topping...and if fresh peaches are in season, use them! Thank you for posting so I didn't lose the trusted recipe!
I made this delicious recipe twice in one week! My husband just loved it. It is best when you refrigerate it before serving as it tastes like an icebox cake too.

When I make it I use self-rising flour insead of the baking mix just because I don't use baking mixes. The co-worker who gave me this receipe always entered it in baking contest. 6 out of 6 times she won the Blue Ribbon.

I took people's suggestions and used the self-rising flour, but I also used cheesecake -flavored Jello to steer it a bit more towards cheesecake. I also didn't add cinnamon or sugar on top, because I wasn't trying to sweeten it anymore that possible. To me cheesecake (or something close) isn't overly sweet. This was very delicious, but my expectations were not that it would be a cheesecake, becuase given the ingredients and the fact that it takes minutes (not hours), should suggest so. I expected more of a cobbler or custard and I got exactly that. In fact, my grandmother used to make this "egg custard" pie and I haven't thought about it in years. When I bit into it it's like my taste buds remembered the texture and equated it somehow. I noticed a bit of negativity towards the texture, but I'm not sure a trained cook should have expected a cheesecake out of this, however the name does suggest such... so it's somwhat fair. I think I'd call it something like Peach Cheesecake Pudding because: This dish is a very Southern summer-time cookout style desert. You can serve it like an alternative to banana pudding with added whipped creme/cool whip and in fact ,I think I'm going to play around with this concept and try banana and/or strawberry. It's great warm like cobbler and its just as good cold like nanner puddin' to me. I'm def going to cook this more and experiment to taste, but this is a fantastic place to start. Thank you for sharing!

I suppose I was expecting it to be sweeter, with a custard like texture. The reviews were all fantastic, but sadly, none of my dinner guests cared for this. Will never make again, and am now hunting for a peaches dish with a custard.
I am not a peach lover but my mom and a coworker loved the cheese cake. It was easy to make and cook.

I had high expectations and made this recipe exactly as it read except for adding a little more peach juice to the batter because it was very dry. But I had to bake it twice as long as the directions suggested since it wasn't set up in the center after 30 minutes. So it came out chewy with more like a dry bread pudding texture than a cheesecake. I won't make this again.

Oh my gosh... I can't possibly say enough good things about this recipe!! Easy to make, every human who has tried it loves it, and we now have to double the recipe just to get a small portion ourselves! This is terrific for home, pot-lucks, anywhere at any time. We actually made this two days in a row because we couldn't get enough! :)
If you like cream cheese danish and peaches..you will LOVE this! I used Jiffy baking mix! Can't stop eating it!
I canned peaches today and had a few left over, so of course I used fresh peaches instead of canned. Needless to say, despite the substitution, it didn't last long in our home. A new fav!
Very good!!! Will decrease the pudding/baking mix layer next time though because I used a 8" pie plate and that part was a bit too thick but otherwise...AWESOME
This dessert was disappointing!!! It sounded good, but it overflowed in my oven, and after cooling was no better. The batter was tough & dry. The cream cheese was gooey. No thanks!
